messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026-459 for inference-gateway-prod-eu-west1 - sustained 5xx rate > 8% over 5m. Link: <https://pagerduty.example/INC-2026-459> Runbook: <https://confluence.example/runbooks/inference-5xx>
pagerduty-bot: Page sent to rotation ops-oncall (attempt 1). Auto-retries enabled. Escalation window 5m.
maya: acked on PD and taking lead. I'm at my desk, pulling dashboards now. Any immediate customer reports?
alex: seeing 502/503 from edge -> gateway -> runtime chain. Error-rate spike started ~02:10 UTC. Top traces show backend runtime returning 502 with "kv cache stall" and occasional OOMs on worker-7.
sam: I'm oncall standby, reachable. Maya, if you want to handoff in 10m I can take it. What mitigations have we tried?
maya: quick summary: we noticed a canary push at 02:08 (commit abc123). I temporarily disabled the canary routing (set CanaryWeight=0) and scaled inference-runtime by +2 replicas a minute ago but errors persisted. Rolling back the canary now.
maya: rolling back canary -> initiating deploy rollback to image redwood/inference:stable-2026-021

```bash
# rollback (runbook step)
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/inference-gateway gateway=redwood/gateway:stable-2026-021
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/inference-gateway
``` 

alex: logs from runtime show repeated lines like:
```
E 02:11:45 runtime_worker.py:KVCacheError: prefix lock timeout
E 02:11:46 runtime_worker.py:AllocError: failed to allocate 640MB
```
so two correlated problems: kvcache contention + memory pressure. Could be bad model shard or malformed request flood.
oncall-r1: checking ingress logs now. I see a small subset of routable paths (batch_predict) getting very high qps with many long seq requests. Likely a traffic pattern shift combined with a bad canary model.
liz: customer-success pinged me; a few large customers reported 5xx and we have one open ticket. We should prepare a short status update for the status page if this becomes >30m incident.
sam: suggestion: enable model fallback for batch_predict route to small-quantized fallback-model, and temporarily reduce max_concurrency per worker. That should relieve mem pressure and reduce error rate.

```yaml
# feature flag change (envoy/filter)
route: /batch_predict
  fallback_model: small-v1-quant
  max_concurrency: 8
``` 

alex: applying fallback now in staging then production. Also kicking KV cache warmup to rebuild prefix hotset.

maya: applied fallback and lowered max_concurrency. Also triggered a cache warmup job for hot prefixes.

```bash
# warmup job
python infra/tools/cache_warmup.py --top-n 2000 --env prod
``` 

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: Ops-SRE rotation paged (severe) after no ack by secondary within 5m.

sam: I'm taking over from maya. I'll coordinate next steps and customer comms. maya handing off — good notes, thanks.
maya: handing off to sam. I'll stay available for context. :thumbsup:

alex: metrics update: 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 5% within 90s of fallback enable. Latency for batch_predict increased slightly but success rate improved.
oncall-r1: still seeing occasional 502s but much reduced. Worker mem OOMs stopped after lowering concurrency.
liz: prepping status page blurb: "We observed elevated 5xx for inference gateway in eu-west1 affecting some customers; mitigation in progress (fallback model + scale). We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Shall I publish now?
sam: yes publish now (short note). Also post to #customer-success so they can reply to tickets.

maya: added short note to status page and pinged CS.

alex: suggest follow-up: run a canary test on abc123 in isolated playground, run mem-profiling on model shard, and add KV cache circuit breaker for prefix lock timeouts.
sam: agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket action/items and assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

```text
Follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: add prefix lock circuit-breaker + better observability (ALLOC failures)  
- eng-ml: repro canary failure, quantize/optimize model shard  
- infra: consider auto-scale buffer for mem pressure spikes
``` 

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-459 acknowledged by maya -> assigned to sam. Incident state: acknowledged, responders engaged.

maya: handing full ownership to sam. I'll update the runbook with times/actions.
sam: taking ownership. I'll keep thread open for monitoring. If 5xx stays <1% for 30m we can close incident and file RCA.

oncall-r1: monitoring dashboards, will alert here on any regression. :eyes:

alex: logs/traces and docker diffs pushed to incident ticket: <https://tickets.example/INC-2026-459>
liz: CS notified customers; I've attached the status page link in the ticket.
sam: thanks team — looks like mitigation worked for now. Keeping watch and will reassign follow-ups. Closing active pager in 30m if stable. :shipit:"
